anti_tick_rules_written_before_any_prose: THE FIX STAYS SHALLOW. NOTHING IS LIFTED TO BE MENDED AND NOTHING UNDER ANYTHING IS OPENED. PACKING GOES UNDER OR AROUND AND THE THING ITSELF STAYS DOWN.

NO CHAPTER ENDS ON THE JOB BEING FINISHED. FOUR END ON A THING LEFT BEHIND AND NOT PUT THERE BY THIS JOB: 0835 THE LICHEN ON THE GATE POST, 0839 THE WEB UNDER THE BRACE, 0841 THE SHAVINGS FROM ANOTHER YEAR, 0844 THE WORN PATCH ON THE STEP. THE OTHER SIX END ON WHAT THE WORK SHOWED.
THE SECOND PERSON IS SHOWN AND NEVER REPORTED. NOBODY IS TOLD, NOBODY IS REFUSED, NOTHING PASSES BETWEEN PEOPLE. THE VISITOR COMES, DOES SOMETHING OF HER OR HIS OWN, AND GOES.
A FIGURE THE CHAPTER ITSELF SETS MUST CLOSE. WHERE A COUNT IS MADE IT IS MADE ONCE AND THE ENDING KEEPS IT.

cards.0835: At number twelve a woman of seventy-eight has a loose flag by the gate that rocked since May and was called sound in spring, and means to pack under it without lifting it; the stop is where the rocking stops, which is packing only and the flag stays down.
cards.0836: At number ten a woman in her early thirties has a butt on its base with the chippings sunk round it, and means to pack chippings back under the rim without moving the butt; the tap above it is left exactly as found and is not run and nothing wet goes near it.
cards.0837: At the lock-up a woman in her late forties has a kerbstone on its rubber that has settled at one end, and means to pack under the low end without lifting the stone; the stop is where the stone sits true and the rubber stays under it.
cards.0838: At number nine a woman in her late fifties has a slab tilted to the rail that stands low at one corner, and means to wedge grit under the low corner without lifting the slab; the stop is where the tilt will take a pail without sliding.
cards.0839: At the unit a man in his early forties has chalk marks on the gate brace gone pale, and means to re-mark the measure the brace already carries; the stop is where the marks read again and no new measure is put on.
cards.0840: At number ten a woman in her early thirties has a gravel hollow under boards on the path, and means to rake the gravel level through the hollow without digging; the stop is where a board lies without rocking.
cards.0841: At the unit a man in his early forties has an oak bench with a twist in it, and means to ease the twist with battens laid under and not cut; the stop is where the bench stands without rocking and no cut is made.
cards.0842: At number nine a woman in her late fifties has pads in the fridge door curled at the edges, and means to lay them flat without replacing them; the stop is where they lie and stay.
cards.0843: At the lock-up a woman in her late forties has a grit rack leg with dust deep round it, and means to sweep round the leg without emptying the rack; the stop is where the leg stands clear and the heap is beside it.
cards.0844: At number twelve a woman of seventy-eight has a brush runner by the front worn thin, and means to lift it and shake the dust out of it without washing it; the stop is where it lies flat again.

movement: Ten jobs, ten sound shallow fixes, ten tired grounds, and nothing opened. 0835 a flag packed without lifting. 0836 chippings packed round a butt without moving it. 0837 packing under a kerbstone without lifting. 0838 grit under a slab without lifting. 0839 marks re-marked without new measure. 0840 gravel raked level without digging. 0841 twist eased without cutting. 0842 pads laid flat without replacing. 0843 dust swept without emptying. 0844 runner shaken without washing. Every job is dry and from the ground.

prohibitions_honoured.everything_dry_and_from_the_ground: Every job is dry and from the ground. No roof, no ladder, no loft, no manhole. No tap run and no water drawn carried poured emptied.
prohibitions_honoured.no_arithmetic_engine: No figure-mismatch spread, no sum worked out to reveal something, no number asked to agree with a number in another chapter. Counting physical things in a single place and letting the count carry the chapter is the trade.
prohibitions_honoured.standing_objects_untouched: The freeholder does not arrive. The line at ten is not put right. The ladder is not opened. The box and its drawers and its lid are not opened. The coal at nine stays shut. No front room is entered. The report is not chased. The envelope is not turned. The bowl stays on its shelf and the ring on the tiles. Ply neither touched nor nailed. The staple is NOT DONE and April is NOT PAGE and the latch stays hooked. Frost NOT TOUCHED. Spanner NOT PICKED. Oval holes NOT FILLED PLUGGED. No cement mortar new concrete. No closed clock and no day tally.

question_put_to_a_human: What are chapters 835 through 844 about, in one sentence? Put to a human before this file was written. No human has answered it for any block from 595 onward. No writer answers it for them. It is recorded here unanswered and it stays open until somebody answers it.

second_measure_done_before_any_prose.method: The ten closings under closing_images were read side by side and three words were written against each one naming what that closing is actually about. Where two descriptions matched the closing was wrong and was rewritten here before the drafting began.
second_measure_done_before_any_prose.result: TEN DESCRIPTIONS, TEN SUBJECTS, NO TWO MATCHING.

still_live_and_taken_up_by_nobody_here: Four pallets on bearers. A shutter that runs silent. A near gate square with a brace in it. A gate on a wall that shuts. A back door shut on its own frame. A cowl braced on a plate. Grass on ground that has not had anything on it. A shelf under a window with a tub on it. Four feet of frost wall with its top course open. A spanner on a set of flags. Six feet of edging in a heap. Off the page and waiting on the man off the ring road, who has now sat out nine blocks: a figure for four rooms given aloud twice in a lock-up and written nowhere; a frame that is out of square; a landing wall with a bare patch; a fourth room at the top of a stair. Three lines of paper shut in a drawer with the tools that would do them. A box in a corner of a lock-up whose lid is not nailed.
